title: The osascript notification fallback delivers a Notification Center entry under Script Editor's identity but paints no banner
detail:
MEASURED on macOS 26.6.1 (Tahoe, M4), run 20260820_143238_macos-26-v2.0.2,
with the screen confirmed clear of consent prompts first (`mac_eyes dialogs`)
- the contamination that invalidated the 2026-08-11 attempt.

THE QUESTION CHANGED SHAPE ONCE THE CODE WAS READ. `_show_macos_notification_un`
already refuses to fall back on an explicit denial: `_un_error_is_denial` ->
log once -> `return True` ("the question is settled"). So the app NEVER reaches
osascript while denied, by design (588bead, product owner's call). The
fallbacks run only on a NON-denial failure, and that is the case worth
measuring.

WHAT osascript ACTUALLY DOES. Screenshot diff (PIL ImageChops.difference +
getbbox) across 0.4s / 0.9s / 1.6s / 2.6s / 4.0s after posting, top-right
region isolated:

    topright bbox = None at every sample, 0 changed pixels

Re-run AFTER the operator enabled notifications: still no banner (the pixel
delta at 1.8s/3.0s was a VS Code redraw - the saved crop shows an editor, not
a notification).

BUT IT IS DELIVERED, NOT DROPPED. The operator opened Notification Center and
photographed it: every probe is present, grouped under a header reading
**"Script Editor"**. That is direct visual confirmation of the identity
objection the product decision rests on - previously only reasoned. A user
would see "Script Editor: Sync done - 12 new files" in their notification
list, attributed to an app they did not run.

SO THE CODE COMMENT OVERSTATES ITS OWN FALLBACK. It says "The only fallback
that could still put a banner on screen in that state is `osascript display
notification`". Measured, osascript does not put a BANNER on screen; it files a
Notification Center ENTRY. The conclusion (respect the denial, do not route
around it) is unaffected and is if anything strengthened by the screenshots.
The premise is what is wrong.

CONFOUNDER, STATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. The operator is on NoMachine and
raised it themselves: "maybe nomachine hides actual notifications though and
runs them straight to notification centre without the popup". That is a real
possibility and this session could not rule it out. A positive control needs an
app with its own bundle identity to banner successfully in the same session;
the packaged app now HAS that identity (the launch prompted, the operator
allowed, Alert Style = Temporary), but making it post requires driving a run to
completion, which did not happen here.

WHAT IS THEREFORE TRUE AND WHAT IS NOT:
  * TRUE  - the fallback is not inert; it delivers a persistent entry.
  * TRUE  - the entry is attributed to Script Editor, visually confirmed.
  * TRUE  - the app does not attempt any fallback while denied.
  * NOT ESTABLISHED - whether osascript can banner on a LOCAL (non-remote)
    macOS 26 session. Do not restate the comment's claim as fact until someone
    measures it at the physical machine.

title: A skip-existing re-download rewrote original_md5 from the on-disk bytes, erasing _NewVersion protection for a same-size local edit
detail:
FOUND 2026-08-20 on the rented Mac while measuring iCloud eviction, then
reproduced against the real class on any platform. The iCloud symptom is what
led here; the data-loss defect is the disease.

`original_md5` means WHAT WE DOWNLOADED. It is the sole basis of
`_classify_local_modification`, which decides 'clean' (safe to overwrite) vs
'modified' (preserve as _NewVersion). `record_downloaded_file` rewrote it from
whatever was on disk.

THE PATH. `record_downloaded_file` runs after EVERY file of a download,
including files SKIPPED because they already existed (core/canvas_logic.py,
"Sync Run #0: Record skipped-but-existing files to the DB"). That call site
passes no local_md5, so the function hashed the on-disk file and stored it.

MEASURED, driving the real class:

    first download        baseline = md5(original bytes)
    student edits it      classification -> 'modified'   (protected)
    re-download course    baseline = md5(THE EDIT)
                          classification -> 'clean'      (NOT protected)

'clean' is the verdict that lets the next sync overwrite the file, and
_NewVersion cannot fire because it reads this row. The edit has to preserve the
file's SIZE (a size change sends the download down the overwrite branch instead
of the skip branch), so it is narrow - but silent, and aimed at the one thing
the product promises about the user's own work.

THE SECOND, CERTAIN COST. Hashing READS the file, and reading an evicted iCloud
file materialises it. Re-running a download over a folder macOS had evicted
pulled the entire course back down: 19 of 19 untouched files, against 0 of 22
for the sync path, on a real iCloud account with a real 22-file Canvas course.

THE FIX needed no new state: `clear_ignored` was already the fresh-vs-skip
discriminator and its docstring already said so. A caller with no md5 is either
recording bytes it just WROTE (clear_ignored=True - secondary HTML/URL renders,
where the file is ours and hashing is correct) or re-recording a skip-existing
file (where it is not). The stored baseline is now preferred whenever one
exists; hashing remains the fallback for a row that has none, which keeps the
original promise that a baseline is never silently dropped.

VERIFIED END TO END on the real evicted iCloud folder: 0 files materialised
after the fix. The single file whose blocks changed was the .webloc, which
_create_link REWRITES every run - our own write, not a fetch, confirmed by its
mtime being seconds old.

COVERED by tests/test_download_baseline_preservation.py (8) and
scripts/_mutate_download_baseline.py - 4/4 caught plus one documented
EQUIVALENT mutant. The mutation pass exposed a real gap in the tests first: a
row that is MISSING and a row that EXISTS WITH AN EMPTY md5 take different
branches, and only the second tells the guards apart.

title: An uninstalled Office app classifies as 'other', not 'app_missing' - three of the four wording clauses were locale-dead
detail: Measured by making osascript fail for real on macOS 26.6.1. A genuinely missing app emits `Can't get application "X". (-1728)` with a TYPOGRAPHIC apostrophe (U+2019); _classify_stderr matched only the ASCII one, and -1728 is not in its numeric list, so the verdict fell through to 'other' - NOT in FATAL_CATEGORIES. Consequence for a user without Microsoft Office (it is not free): no 'Word is not installed' message. Three generic per-file errors, then SYSTEMIC_REPEAT_THRESHOLD fires and tells them to 'Quit Microsoft Word and run again' - about an app they do not have. Same class one clause over: this machine's macOS also emits the BRITISH 'Not authorised to send Apple events', while the permission clause knew only 'authorized'; that verdict survived solely on its -1743 companion. Only 'isn't running' worked, because the 2026-08-11 -600 fix gave that one clause both apostrophe forms and never reached its neighbours. FIXED by normalising the apostrophe ONCE (so a future clause cannot inherit the bug) plus adding the British spelling. -1728 deliberately NOT added to the numeric list: our own scripts raise errAENoSuchObject for an absent DOCUMENT, so mapping the code wholesale would abort a phase with 'Office is not installed' on a machine where it plainly is - a mutant pins that. tests/test_office_crash_is_not_missing.py; scripts/_mutate_applescript_locale.py, 6/6 caught.

title: A denied 'access data from other apps' prompt reads as a slow document: ~4 minutes per file and no cause named
oracles: the debug log vs Word's own open-document path
detail: Measured in the PACKAGED app by clicking Don't Allow on 'Canvas Downloader would like to access data from other apps' - a state nothing had driven, and an ordinary one, since the wording gives a cautious student no reason to accept. ONE .doc cost ~4 minutes (2 attempts x ~2 min timeout) and reported only 'AppleEvent timed out (-1712)' then 'Conversion failed twice' - naming neither the cause nor a remedy. On a 30-file course that is hours of apparent hang. MECHANISM confirmed rather than inferred: Word was left holding the ORIGINAL path (Macintosh HD:private:tmp:...), not a staged src_* one - so the denial made _office_container_tmp answer None, office_container_stage fell back to _direct_passthrough, and Word was asked to open a file OUTSIDE its container, which raises the per-folder powerbox prompt THAT STAGING EXISTS TO AVOID; a blocked prompt holds the AppleEvent until timeout. office_container_stage's docstring called that degrade 'never worse than before, only ever better', and the trap note in the same function already described this exact mechanism - as a hazard for anyone re-MEASURING staging, without noticing it is a live USER path. FIXED: the fallback records itself (_office_unstaged, per-run), and attribute_office_failure refines a stderr-only verdict with it - a timeout while unstaged becomes 'container_denied', which is FATAL so the phase aborts once. Deliberately narrow: a timeout WITH staging stays a per-file 'other', and only timeouts qualify, so a wedged Word (-1708) or mis-bound document (-30001) is not blamed on permissions. The remedy names FULL DISK ACCESS, not 'Files and Folders' - checked in System Settings with the denial recorded, the app appears there with NO TOGGLE, while FDA supersedes the grant and is the pane the app's own nudge already opens. No data loss at any point: the .doc survived, no stub PDF, 0 staged dirs. tests/test_container_denied_attribution.py (16); scripts/_mutate_container_denied.py, 8/8 caught - after the pass exposed 4 weak tests of mine that re-implemented the rule instead of calling it.
scenario: M-new, packaged app, powerbox DENIED, macOS 26.6.1

title: The macOS Keychain ACL prompt ran on the SCRIPT THREAD, so an app update left the window empty for up to 90 seconds with nothing explaining why
detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 in the PACKAGED app on macOS 26.6.1.

restore_saved_session() runs on the Streamlit script thread during init, before
anything renders, and keyring's macOS backend calls SecItemCopyMatching with NO
UI-suppression flag. When the saved item's ACL does not trust the running binary
that call BLOCKS on a system prompt, so the script never finishes and the
frontend has nothing to render.

WHAT THE USER SAW (frames captured):
  0-30s   boot overlay: 'Connecting...' + spinner
  30-90s  the overlay's absolute cap fires and the window is COMPLETELY EMPTY
  on Deny / 90s watchdog: the login page, with NO explanation at all
Nothing connected the empty window to the Keychain dialog, and on macOS
_load_fallback_token is a deliberate no-op, so a denial silently means 'find a
Canvas token again'.

IT FIRES ON EVERY APP UPDATE: the bundle is ad-hoc signed (TeamIdentifier not
set) and BOTH halves of a keychain item's access control key on the signature.

TWO ESCAPES MEASURED AND CLOSED, so nobody re-derives them:
  * security add-generic-password -A (trusted-app list <null>) STILL prompts -
    the ACL dump shows partition_id 'apple-tool:', and the partition list gates
    access independently of the trusted-app list.
  * The app cannot silently repair its own ACL after the user allows: the delete
    half of delete+add needs authorisation we do not have and fails -25244. It
    fails SAFELY (the item survives), which is why the attempt is UI-suppressed.

THE FOOT-GUN, measured by re-reading with UI suppressed after each click:
  Allow        -> ACL UNCHANGED -> prompts on EVERY LAUNCH, forever
  Always Allow -> ACL UPDATED   -> silent until the next update
Which button the user presses is the difference between one prompt per update
and one prompt for ever - and nothing told them.

FIXED. keyring_get_without_prompting() probes with keychain UI suppressed (4.3ms
on success, 9.6ms when a prompt would be needed - both measured), so init can
never block. When a prompt IS required the login screen paints immediately,
explains the dialog in the user's terms, and raises the prompt from a daemon
thread as the LAST thing on the page - so the dialog lands on a painted,
self-explaining window. A 1Hz fragment adopts the answer, so the user never
touches the app.

VERIFIED END TO END in the real app on this machine:
  after update, prompt up : painted login page + notice in 1.12s
  user clicks Always Allow: app signs ITSELF in, zero app interaction
  next launch             : signed in in 1.15s, no notice, no dialog at all
  ACL after Always Allow  : suppressed read succeeds, needs_prompt False

A SECOND DEFECT was found by driving the real app rather than by the tests: the
unlock state is process-global (a background thread has no ScriptRunContext)
while keychain_unlock_pending is per SESSION, so consuming the resolved token
left a second session (a reload, or a second window) with an empty token, no
notice and a bare login page. Observed; the token is now kept for the process
and cleared by logout/force_reauth.

COVERED by tests/test_keychain_unlock.py (33) and
scripts/_mutate_keychain_unlock.py - 23/23 caught. Two survivors in the first
pass were real gaps in my own tests: counting keychain READS is not a test of
single-flight (the workers serialise on the UI lock, so one read happens either
way - count THREADS), and nothing checked app.py's call site at all, so deleting
the adoption call while leaving its import satisfied every test.
scenario: packaged app, post-update Keychain ACL prompt, macOS 26.6.1
